description: A 25 by 25 grid of magnetic spins flipping under a simulated temperature: the grid is split into twenty-five zones and each zone's average alignment comes out as a voltage

params.text: Sets how much random flipping the spins do against the pull of their neighbours, none at one end of the travel to constant churn at the other
Biases the spins toward one alignment or the other, -1 to 1, and is the mixture a reset starts from
Sets how strongly a spin is pulled to match its neighbours, none at one end of the travel to the full amount at the other
Sets the time between spin updates, 0.15ms to 2ms, so turning it clockwise slows the lattice down despite the panel printing RATE
Attenuverts the temperature CV before it is added to the temperature knob
Attenuverts the polarity CV before it is added to the polarity knob
Attenuverts the interaction CV before it is added to the interaction knob
Scatters every spin afresh on each press, with the mixture of alignments set by the polarity control

inputs.text: Writes into the central five-by-five block of the grid, pulling it one way at -5V and the other at 5V, from where it spreads outward; it is added to the polarity as well
A rise scatters every spin afresh, with the mixture of alignments set by the polarity control
Changes the temperature, scaled by a tenth and added to the temperature knob through its attenuverter, the total clamped to the knob's travel
Changes the polarity, scaled by a tenth and added to the polarity knob through its attenuverter, the total clamped to -1 to 1
Changes the interaction strength, scaled by a tenth and added to the interaction knob through its attenuverter, the total clamped to the knob's travel

outputs.text: The average alignment of that zone of the grid, smoothed by four stages of low-pass filtering, from -10V to 10V or half that on the menu setting

notes: the grid keeps moving on its own: the temperature drives random flips whether or not anything is patched, and the outputs wander with it
the central zone of the twenty-five has no jack; that block of the grid is the one the tape head writes into
menu: Voltage Range ±5V — halves every zone output, so the grid swings between -5V and 5V rather than -10V and 10V
